What we fix

London is one of the hardest water areas in the country, and scale inside the cartridge or the thermostatic cell is behind most shower faults here. We find the cause before we change anything.

01
Runs hot then cold

The classic thermostatic fault: a scaled or worn cartridge that can no longer hold temperature.

02
Scalding when a tap is run

The thermostatic cell has stopped compensating, which is a safety issue as well as a nuisance.

03
Stuck on the temperature stop

The override or maximum stop seized with scale, so you cannot get the heat you want.

04
Low or dropping pressure

Checked across the cartridge, the head and the feed, in that order, before anything is replaced.

05
A dripping shower

A shower that will not fully shut off, which is a worn cartridge or a perished seal.

06
A leaking valve or head

The leak found and stopped before it reaches the ceiling below.

07
Noisy or juddering

Knocking or juddering under load, usually pressure balance or a failing part.

08
A blocked shower head

Scaled up so the spray pattern has gone, descaled or replaced.

09
Replace a thermostatic valve

The exact cartridge or cell matched to the make and model, not a near-enough substitute.

We work on thermostatic, mixer and digital showers from Mira, Aqualisa, Grohe and Hansgrohe, bar and concealed valves, cartridges and thermostatic cells, hoses, heads and diverters, on both stored and combi hot water feeds. On a concealed valve we work through the trim wherever possible, so the tiling is not disturbed.

Got a different type of shower? We cover mixer shower repairs, electric shower repairs and power shower repairs on their own pages.

Different job? For water escaping at the tray see resealing baths and shower trays, for a leak you cannot find see sourcing and curing leaks, and for a new screen see bath and shower screen installation.

What it costs

Labour only, charged by time, plus parts. A common fault such as a worn thermostatic cartridge or a leaking seal is usually diagnosed inside the first 30 to 60 minutes, so a typical one-hour repair is £90 plus VAT plus parts.

Shower repair FAQs
Can you repair my shower today in London?

Often yes. Silver Saints usually has same or next day slots for shower repair in London, and every booking carries a one-hour arrival window.

Why does my thermostatic shower run hot then cold?

Usually a worn or scaled thermostatic cartridge. Silver Saints descales or replaces it and checks the shower holds temperature when another outlet is run.

My shower scalds when someone runs a tap. Is that dangerous?

It can be. The thermostatic cell has stopped compensating, and Silver Saints replaces it so the shower protects against a sudden temperature swing.

How much does a shower repair cost in London?

Charged by time at £60 plus VAT for the first 30 minutes and £30 plus VAT thereafter, so a typical one-hour repair is £90 plus VAT plus parts.

Why has my shower lost pressure?

It could be the cartridge, the head or the feed. Silver Saints checks all three in order rather than replacing parts on guesswork.

My shower drips and will not turn off. Can you fix it?

Yes. That is almost always a worn cartridge or a perished seal, and Silver Saints replaces it with the correct part for your make and model.

Are you a job-board app like the marketplaces?

We are not a job-board app. Unlike marketplaces that match your job to the cheapest available bidder, Silver Saints contracts its own team of experienced, vetted, multi-skilled tradespeople, people we know personally and work with directly. From booking to billing, you get one accountable service and a real relationship, not an anonymous login from a gig-economy pool.

Is it worth repairing a shower or replacing it?

Most faults are a worn part that costs far less to repair. Silver Saints will tell you plainly when a shower is beyond economic repair.

In summary

Silver Saints repair thermostatic and mixer showers across London. We fix temperatures that run hot then cold, showers that scald when a tap is run, seized temperature stops, low and dropping pressure, dripping and leaking valves and heads, noisy or juddering showers and blocked heads, and we replace cartridges, thermostatic cells and valves with the exact part for the make and model. London hard water is behind most of it. Labour is £60 plus VAT for the first 30 minutes, then £30 plus VAT thereafter, plus parts, so a typical one-hour repair is £90 plus VAT plus parts. Saturday is the weekday rate and there is no call-out fee. Call 0207 0999 199 or book at https://bookings.silversaints.com.

Repairs and faults
What we fix on a mixer shower

Stiff controls, a weeping head and a temperature that will not settle all come back to the same few parts. We strip the valve and match the exact cartridge rather than guessing.

01
Stiff or grinding controls

A lever or knob that has seized with scale, freed off or the cartridge replaced.

02
A weeping head or spout

Water still running when it is off, which is a worn cartridge or perished O-rings.

03
Too hot or too cold

The cartridge can no longer balance the hot and cold supplies, so the mix drifts.

04
Scaled inlet filters

Grit and scale in the filters choking the flow, cleared as part of the service.

05
A scaled valve body

Descaled where it will recover, replaced where it will not.

06
Bar mixer service

Cartridge and inlet filters, the two usual service points on an exposed bar valve.

07
Concealed valve repair

Done through the trim wherever possible, so the tiling is not disturbed.

08
Perished O-rings and seals

Replaced as a set, so you are not back to the same drip in three months.

09
Diverter faults

Water going to the head and the spout at once, or refusing to switch between them.

We isolate the hot and cold supplies, strip the valve, descale or replace the cartridge and seals, check the inlet filters for grit and scale, then rebuild and test so the controls move freely and the temperature holds before we leave.

Mixer showers are common in London period conversions and mansion blocks fed from a stored hot water system, where balanced hot and cold pressures matter, and in modern flats running off a mains-pressure combi.

Not a mixer? See electric shower repairs, power shower repairs, or the main shower repairs page. This can be combined in one visit with resealing the bath or shower tray or replacing a worn tap.
